Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1500
Claimant:
Lisa Mack
Adjuster:
Jerry Hanson
2024-07-27
First notice of loss received from the insured's policyholder regarding a low-speed head-on collision. The claimant
reports a back strain and is represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.
2024-08-18
Verified the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of the loss. Nothing in the file
suggests the damage predates the policy start.
2024-08-19
Police report obtained. It confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of impact, and the responding officer's
account matches the insured's description of the collision.
2024-09-04
Statements taken from two witnesses and the other driver. All three describe the accident the same way as the
insured, and scene photos are consistent with that account.
2024-11-07
Vehicle inspection completed. The impact damage fits a low-speed head-on collision. A few older scratches are
visible on the bumper, and it is not yet clear whetehr all of the damage came from this impact, so a repair estimate is
pending a closer look.
2024-12-01
Medical records received from the claimant's treating provider. The reported back strain fits the kind and force of this
crash well, and no prior injury to the same body area is known.
2025-02-11
Claimant's attorney sent a supplemental statement adding a few small details about the moment of impact. The core
account is unchanged from the initial report.
2025-02-26
Treatment records show a usual course of care that tapered off as the patient improved. Requested updated provider
notes to confirm current status and whether any further treatment is expected.
2025-03-04
File reviewed with the claimant's counsel in place. Next steps are to finalize the repair estimate, reconcile the older
scratches against the impact damage, and reassess the bodily injury claim once the latest treatment notes arrive.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
